question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s dominant position within the Chinese Communist Party and military underpins the 95.3% implied probability that he remains in office through 2026. Extensive purges of senior PLA and Politburo figures since early 2026, including investigations of close allies, have reinforced loyalty and centralized decision-making ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027. At age 73, Xi has shown no public signals of retirement or successor designation, while maintaining an active international schedule and policy focus on party discipline, technological self-reliance, and national security. The “wisdom of crowds” reflected in current pricing aligns with the absence of visible elite challenges or procedural mechanisms for removal before the congress. Unlikely but plausible shifts could still arise from sudden health developments, a major external crisis, or unexpected internal dissent that alters elite calculations.
